correctness.rationale: On connected graphs U^2x=x implies the two-round firing-total vector is a constant harmonic integer vector. Primitive period two forces exactly one firing per vertex, giving complementary firing sets. Direct threshold inequalities give a one-to-one cut/slack parametrization, exact cut polynomial and full contiguous interval for each feasible cut. Every maximizing cut has positive cross degree, and its mass interval contains all others. Endpoint uniqueness, reciprocity and polynomial-time MAX-CUT reduction follow. Full checked domain n>=2; the two independently implemented stdlib programs replayed successfully and test 771 labelled connected graphs and 139 additional constructive examples.

value.rationale: The result determines the complete natural chip-mass support on all finite connected simple graphs and exactly counts both boundary populations by maximum-cut multiplicity. It turns a recurrent-state invariant into a classical global graph optimization invariant and gives an NP-complete decision problem with an exact reduction, rather than a graph-family substitution or recomputation of earlier tables. It provides a structural tool for understanding energy support even when interior coefficients remain unknown.
